english.notes:
This offence wording is now OBSOLETE - repealed the Statue Law (Repeals) Act 2008

(i) A disorderly house is a house kept open, not necessarily to the public at large, and so conducted as to violate law and good order. Where the essence of the charge is the presentation of an indecent performance, a conviction for keeping a disorderly house will be supported, although there is no evidence of indecency or disorderly conduct perceptible from the exterior of the house. Section 8 of the Disorderly Houses Act 1751 provides that any person who appears, acts or behaves as master or mistress or as the person having the care, government or management of a disorderly house shall be deemed to be the keeper. (In Archbold this legislation is treated as different to the Common Law offence which can be viewed as a separate charge wording at H2155.)
(ii) The owner of a house, letting it out in different apartments to several young women, who use the apartments for the purposes of prostitution, cannot be indicted for keeping a disorderly house. Brothel keeping is normally prosecuted under section 33 of the Sexual Offences Act 1956 - see offence wordings H550 and H554.
